title: The Price Column and the Crown Prince: Menger from Galicia to the Zentralfriedhof
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Nowy Sacz, the birth in Neu-Sandez
stops.date_confidence: contested. The University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie independently give 23 February 1840; the Mises Institute biography prints 28 February, the older and widely reprinted variant. Neither date has been checked here against a parish register. Coordinate is the old-town Rynek, corrected from a figure that fell some 700 m south toward the Dunajec. The tradition that he was born around noon is family reconstruction and carries no documentary weight.
stops.campa: In the Galician town the Habsburgs call Neu-Sandez, on the Dunajec, a son is born to the lawyer Anton Menger and Caroline Gerzabek and christened Carl Eberhart Anton. The family carries the noble particle von Wolfensgruen; the sons will lay it down in their manhood as a profession of bourgeois conviction. Two institutions that keep his record, the University of Vienna and the Neue Deutsche Biographie, put the day at the twenty-third of February. A third, printed and reprinted for a century, says the twenty-eighth. The register that would settle it has not been produced.
suggested_refs: Parish registers of Nowy Sacz for February 1840, not consulted in this pass
Neue Deutsche Biographie, entry Menger, Carl (GND 118580841)
sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at/en/persons/carl-menger-von-wolfensgruen
Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html
Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger (for the 28 February variant)
Wikipedia, 'Nowy Sacz' (town coordinates)

stops.name: Biala, the smoke of the father's law office
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The relocation to Biala, the elementary schooling there from 1843, and the childhood hours in Anton Menger's office come from the family-archival reconstruction, chiefly Karl Menger's unpublished draft biography as relayed through the Duke papers scholarship. No independent primary source was reached. The date is set to 1843 only to order the segment.
stops.campa: The household moves west to Biala, a cloth town on the Silesian border, and the boy starts elementary school there in 1843. He grows up in the smoke of his father's law office, among deeds and contracts and the plain arithmetic of what a thing is worth to the man who wants it. Anton Menger arbitrates between weavers and merchants, and his sons hear the prices argued at the table. Property, in this house, is not a word out of a book. It is a stack of paper with names on it. He is three years old when they arrive.
stops.quote: The entire sum of goods at an economizing individual's command for the satisfaction of his needs, we call his property. His property is not, however, an arbitrarily combined quantity of goods, but a direct reflection of his needs, an integrated whole, no essential part of which can be diminished or increased without affecting realization of the end it serves.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. James Dingwall and Bert F. Hoselitz, Chapter I section 6, p. 76
suggested_refs: Karl Menger's draft biography of his father, Carl Menger Papers, Duke University
sources: Family-archival reconstruction via the Carl Menger Papers scholarship at Duke; not independently corroborated

stops.name: Maniowy, the mother's land above the Dunajec
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Gerzabek estate, the boy's presence there, and the story that the tenants stood by the household during the 1846 Galician rising are family tradition only. Coordinate corrected by roughly 5.5 km to the present relocated village; the original settlement lay lower and to the south and is now under the Czorsztyn reservoir. Dam resolution 1964, resettlement through the 1970s and 1980s, inundation of the old town 1995.
stops.campa: At the Gerzabek land at Maniowy, above the Dunajec, the boy watches the working of a small economy that has no theory of itself: peasants bringing grain, craftsmen setting a price, the weekly market assembling and dispersing. Family memory holds that in the Galician rising of 1846, when landlords elsewhere were killed by their own peasants, the tenants here stood around the house. The village he knew is gone. The dam resolution passed in 1964, the people were moved through the seventies and eighties, and in 1995 the water closed over the old town.
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'Maniowy', on the resettlement and the Czorsztyn reservoir
sources: Family-archival reconstruction, not independently corroborated
Wikipedia, 'Maniowy' (coordinates and inundation chronology)

stops.name: Cieszyn, the Gymnasium at Teschen
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Teschen Gymnasium years 1851 to 1857, the boarding arrangements, and the curriculum are family-archival reconstruction; Britannica and the general reference works confirm a Gymnasium education without naming Teschen. Britannica itself returned HTTP 403 in this pass and could not be read directly. Month set to September to order the segment.
stops.campa: He boards in Teschen with women who rent rooms to schoolboys and takes the Catholic German Gymnasium's curriculum: Latin, Greek, French, history, and a mathematics that stops well short of the calculus. The economics he will make has no derivatives in it and never needed any; value in his account is not a slope but a rank, the order in which a man would give up what he has. Nothing in this classroom prepares that. He is taught to construe a sentence and to keep his seat.
suggested_refs: Records of the Catholic German Gymnasium at Teschen, 1851-1857
sources: Family-archival reconstruction, not independently corroborated

stops.name: Krakow, the final school year and the graduation
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction for the Krakow year and the cum laude; the 1859 start of university study is attested by the Mises Institute biography, which gives the university span as 1859 to 1863. The intervening Gymnasium year at Troppau, 1857-1858, is likewise family reconstruction and is not carried as a separate stop. Month set to June to order the segment.
stops.campa: The last Gymnasium year is taken in Krakow, the old royal capital in Galicia's other half, and he graduates cum laude. He is nineteen. Three brothers of one Galician lawyer's family are now pointed at Vienna: Carl to economics, Anton to law and the socialist critique of the civil code, Max to politics. None of them will keep the particle their father's title gave them. Carl, who will spend his working life explaining why a thing has the value it has, sets down without argument a name worth something at any Austrian door.
suggested_refs: German Wikipedia, 'Carl Menger', on the brothers' renunciation of von Wolfensgruen
sources: Family-archival reconstruction for the Krakow year
de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Menger, on the laying down of the title as a profession of bourgeois conviction

stops.name: Vienna, matriculation at the Alte Universitaet
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1859 start of study at Vienna (Mises Institute biography, span 1859-1863). The building attribution is now source-backed rather than inferred: the university did not move to the Ringstrasse until 1884. Coordinate corrected by about 170 m to the Alte Universitaet on Dr.-Ignaz-Seipel-Platz. The named lecturers Carl Ludwig Arndts and Heinrich Siegel could not be verified, since Britannica returned HTTP 403, and are omitted from the prose.
stops.campa: He matriculates in law and state sciences at the old Jesuit college on the square the university has occupied since the fourteenth century and will not leave until 1884. Vienna in 1859 is a liberal city under a shaken emperor: Solferino lost that summer, the constitution being redrafted, the walls about to come down. The state sciences are taught here as a branch of administration, preparation for men who will govern an empire of many nations and one treasury. Nobody in the faculty is teaching that value is a fact about a person rather than a property of a thing.
suggested_refs: University of Vienna matriculation registers, winter semester 1859
sources: Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger
de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alte_Universitaet_(Wien), for the site and the 1884 move

stops.name: Prague, the Karolinum and the first state examination
stops.date_confidence: the Prague law study 1860-1863 rests on Britannica, which could not be re-fetched in this pass (HTTP 403) and is carried at reduced confidence. The teachers Alois von Brinz and Johann Friedrich von Schulte and the cum laude in Roman law are dossier detail. The fraternity duel and the scar are family reconstruction with no independent record and no known venue; the fencing hall is not named anywhere reached. Month set to October to order the segment.
stops.campa: He continues at Prague, in the Karolinum, taking Roman law and canon law and passing the first state examination in Roman law with distinction. Prague in these years is a city arguing in two languages about which one it is, and the Galician-born German student stands where his schooling put him. He is twenty-one and means to be a lawyer. In student fashion he also fences with a German fraternity, and what he carries away from that is a small scar on the left side of his nose.
suggested_refs: Charles University law faculty examination records, 1860-1863
sources: Britannica, 'Carl Menger' (cited by the dossier; page returned HTTP 403 here and could not be re-read)
Family-archival reconstruction for the duel and the scar

stops.name: Lviv, editing the Lemberger Zeitung
stops.date_confidence: attested that he worked as a journalist in Lviv (Britannica, as cited by the dossier; the page itself returned HTTP 403 in this pass). The specific title Lemberger Zeitung, the editorial rank, and the dating to the mid-1860s are dossier detail not independently confirmed. Day and month defaulted to 01-01.
stops.campa: He works as an editor on the Lemberger Zeitung, the official paper of Galicia's capital, in a city of Poles, Ruthenians, Germans, Armenians and Jews where four rites of Christianity keep churches within a few streets of the market square. The work is unsigned and mostly lost. What survives of it is the habit: a man paid to read a province's commerce and render it in a column, day after day. The office address is not recorded and no list of what he wrote there exists.
suggested_refs: Runs of the Lemberger Zeitung for the mid-1860s, unexamined
sources: Britannica, 'Carl Menger' (journalism in Lviv; page not re-readable here)

stops.name: Vienna, the press district and Count Belcredi
stops.date_confidence: attested that Menger met Minister-President Richard Belcredi in 1865 (Mises Institute biography); the brief work for the Botschafter and Die Presse is uncorroborated dossier detail. Source error corrected: the Mises biography calls Belcredi a Liberal, which inverts his politics. Belcredi was a declared Conservative, Minister-President from 27 July 1865 to 7 February 1867, installed against Schmerling's Liberal centralism. Month set to June to order the segment.
stops.campa: Back in Vienna he takes brief work for the semi-official Botschafter and for the liberal Die Presse, and in the same year meets the Minister-President, Count Richard Belcredi. The biography that carries the meeting calls Belcredi a Liberal. He was the opposite: a declared Conservative installed in July 1865 to undo Schmerling's centralizing constitution, which he governed by suspending. So the young journalist is noticed by the man dismantling the liberal state. Belcredi holds office until the seventh of February 1867.
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'Richard Belcredi', on his conservatism and his term of office
sources: Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger (for the meeting, and for the miscalled politics)
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Belcredi (correcting the political label)

stops.name: Vienna, the one-kreuzer daily
stops.date_confidence: the venture is externally attested: German Wikipedia records Menger as co-editor of the newly founded Neues Wiener Tagblatt from 1865 to 1866. The paper's exact name varies between sources (Wiener Tagblatt, Neues Wiener Tagesblatt, Neues Wiener Tagblatt) and is not resolved here. The ornaments remain reconstruction: the partner Ignaz von Lackenbacher, the one-kreuzer price, the circulation of about 35,000, the market halls and prison reform, and the ministry's purchase in February 1866. The day-level founding date of 26 November is dossier detail.
stops.campa: A new daily appears in Vienna at one kreuzer, cheap enough for a servant, financed by advertising rather than by subscription, and Menger is its co-editor. The paper argues for public market halls, cheap information, and reform of the prisons. Circulation is said to reach thirty-five thousand before the model fails and the ministry buys the title in February. He has tried to sell information at something near the cost of producing it. He is twenty-five when the paper stops being his.
suggested_refs: Surviving issues of the Neues Wiener Tagblatt, November 1865 to February 1866
sources: de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Menger, 'From 1865-1866, he served as co-editor of the newly founded Neues Wiener Tagesblatt'
Dossier press-history reconstruction for the price, circulation, programme and sale

stops.name: Vienna, the economic section of the Wiener Zeitung
stops.date_confidence: corrected. The dossier read its own source backwards: the Mises Institute biography gives autumn 1866 as the moment Menger departed the official newspaper to prepare for his doctoral examination, which makes 1866 the end of the Wiener Zeitung period and not its start. The systematic market analysis dated 1871-1875 belongs to a different post and is carried at its own stop. The claim that the price columns stimulated his value theory is his own later report and his students', not an independent record. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: In the economic section of the Wiener Zeitung he works the raw material directly: price lists, market reports, quotations from the exchange, the daily record of what people actually paid. In the autumn of 1866 he leaves the official paper to prepare for the doctoral examination. What he takes with him is a discrepancy he cannot put down. The prices in the columns do not behave as the textbooks on his shelf say they should. The textbooks are by respected men. The columns are the world.
stops.quote: Things that can be placed in a causal connection with the satisfaction of human needs we term useful things. If, however, we both recognize this causal connection, and have the power actually to direct the useful things to the satisfaction of our needs, we call them goods.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter I section 1, p. 52
suggested_refs: Runs of the Wiener Zeitung economic section, 1865-1866
sources: Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger (departure in autumn 1866)
Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz

stops.name: Krakow, the doctorate in law at the Collegium Maius
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the institution by the Neue Deutsche Biographie and the University of Vienna faculty history, both giving a Dr. iur. from Krakow in 1867. The month is unknown and defaulted to January. The claim that an unresolved dispute with the Prague dean kept him from sitting the oral doctorate at Charles University is dossier reconstruction, resting on an undated polemical manuscript, and is not asserted.
stops.campa: He returns to Krakow to sit examinations and takes the doctorate in law from the Jagiellonian, in the Collegium Maius, where the university has kept its oldest rooms since the fourteenth century. It is a lawyer's degree. Every academic post he will hold, and the Vienna chair itself, rests on a qualification in a subject he is about to leave for good. In economics, the field in which he founds a school, he is self-taught and holds no degree at all. The month of the promotion is not on record.
suggested_refs: Jagiellonian University promotion records for 1867
sources: Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html
University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at

stops.name: Vienna, the apprentice turns to economics
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Mises Institute biography, which dates the entry into apprentice legal practice to May 1867 and the beginning of intensive dedicated study of economics to September 1867. The reading list is not documented; no source reached names which authors he worked through in these years. The exact residence is unknown and the coordinate is a general Vienna pin.
stops.campa: In May he enters apprentice legal practice, as an Austrian law graduate is expected to. By September he has begun the intensive private study of economics that will not stop until there is a book. He reads the German textbook economists and the classical school standing behind them, and he reads against them, because the thing he saw in the price columns is not in any of them. He has no chair, no supervisor and no funding. Which authors he actually worked through in those four years is nowhere written down.
stops.quote: This is the ground on which I stand. In what follows I have endeavored to reduce the complex phenomena of human economic activity to the simplest elements that can still be subjected to accurate observation, to apply to these elements the measure corresponding to their nature, and constantly adhering to this measure, to investigate the manner in which the
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Author's Preface, p. 46. The sentence runs onto the following page, which was not captured; it is quoted only to the point actually read. Menger wrote in editorial 'we', silently converted to 'I' by the translators, per their own footnote on the same page.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger's reading notes of 1867-1871, Carl Menger Papers, Duke University
sources: Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger
Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz

stops.name: Vienna, the market analyst in the press office
stops.date_confidence: attested that Menger was appointed to the Austrian cabinet press department in 1870 (Mises Institute biography). German Wikipedia dates the systematic observation and analysis of the market situation in the Ministerratspraesidium press office to about 1871. The dossier had folded this work back into the Wiener Zeitung years and dated it 1871-1875 there; that is the error corrected. Day and month defaulted to 01-01.
stops.campa: He enters the civil service, in the press department of the Ministerratspraesidium, and is set to the systematic observation and analysis of the market situation for the government's own use. The job is to know what the empire's prices are doing and to say so in writing. He is being paid, in effect, to keep doing the thing that produced the problem, and he uses the office as a laboratory. The book gets written in the margins of the official work, at night, over four years.
stops.quote: All things are subject to the law of cause and effect. This great principle knows no exception, and we would search in vain in the realm of experience for an example to the contrary.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter I section 1, p. 51, the opening sentence of the book
suggested_refs: Ministerratspraesidium press office files, 1870-1875
sources: Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger
de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Menger (systematische Beobachtung und Analyse der Marktlage)

stops.name: Vienna, Grundsaetze der Volkswirthschaftslehre
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by the University of Vienna faculty history and the Econlib biography. The month is not established here and is defaulted to January. The pin is the Alte Universitaet, the university's site at the date, though the book was written in the press office and at home rather than in the faculty; no residence address was reached. The simultaneous discoveries by Jevons and Walras are omitted, since no source in the verified pool carries them.
stops.campa: Braumueller of Vienna publishes Grundsaetze der Volkswirthschaftslehre, a small book by an unknown official, and it does what its author intended. It takes economic life apart down to a single acting person with needs, a stock of goods, and knowledge of what depends on what. Value is not in the wheat. Value is the importance the man attaches to the wheat because he is conscious of depending on it. The book sells modestly, is never reprinted in his lifetime by his own refusal, and waits seventy-nine years for an English translation.
stops.quote: Never was there an age that placed economic interests higher than does our own. Never was the need of a scientific foundation for economic affairs felt more generally or more acutely.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Author's Preface, p. 45, the opening paragraph of the 1871 preface
suggested_refs: Grundsaetze der Volkswirthschaftslehre, Vienna: Wilhelm Braumueller, 1871, first edition
sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at

stops.name: Vienna, the trial lecture and the first chair
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1872 habilitation and the 1873 associate professorship by the University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie, which give 1873 and, in the Mises account, September 1873. The failed trial lecture, Lorenz von Stein's resistance, the credit-and-banking course, the forty students, and the declined posts at Wiener Neustadt, Karlsruhe and Basel are dossier detail, not independently corroborated. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: The trial lecture fails at the first attempt and Lorenz von Stein, who holds the field in Vienna, resists him. He qualifies as Privatdozent in political economy nonetheless, one year after the book, and his first course, on credit and banking, draws about forty students. In September 1873 he is made ausserordentlicher Professor, having declined posts at Wiener Neustadt, Karlsruhe and Basel. He is thirty-three, and the school that will be named after a country rather than after a man exists so far as one lecturer and a course list.
stops.quote: Value is thus the importance that individual goods or quantities of goods attain for us because we are conscious of being dependent on command of them for the satisfaction of our needs.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter III section 1, p. 115
suggested_refs: University of Vienna habilitation file for Carl Menger, 1872
sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at
Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html
Mises Institute, biography of Carl Menger

stops.name: Vienna, tutor to the heir
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1876 by the University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie, both of which give only the year. The day-level date of 3 January appears in neither and is dossier detail. The Hofburg as lesson venue is the dossier's own acknowledged inference. Age corrected: Rudolf was born 21 August 1858 and was seventeen in January 1876, not eighteen. The examination before Franz Joseph in June 1876 and the count of roughly three hundred dinners are uncorroborated.
stops.campa: On Joseph Latour's recommendation the professor is set to teach the heir to the throne. Rudolf is seventeen, quick, liberal by temperament, and in a position where a liberal temperament is a private embarrassment. Menger takes him through theoretical economics, policy, finance and statistics, sometimes four hours in a day, and the two of them get on. The Crown Prince is examined before his father the Emperor and passes. Over the years that follow, tutor and pupil will dine together something near three hundred times.
suggested_refs: Crown Prince Rudolf's study notebooks and Menger's lesson papers, Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv, Vienna
sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at
Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf,_Crown_Prince_of_Austria (birth date, correcting the age)

stops.name: Goedoelloe, the lessons follow the court
stops.date_confidence: the court context is solid: Franz Joseph and the royal family spent several months at Goedoelloe every year from 1867 to 1918. Menger's own presence there, and the remark about the Order of the Iron Crown Third Class, are dossier reconstruction with no independent record. Coordinate corrected by about 650 m to the palace itself. The date is set to September 1876 only to order the segment within the 1876-1888 span.
stops.campa: The court removes to Hungary for months at a stretch, to the great baroque house at Goedoelloe that Franz Joseph and Elisabeth were given at the Compromise, and the lessons go with it. Menger is now inside court society: a Galician lawyer's son among archdukes, teaching the future emperor how prices form. He is given the Order of the Iron Crown, Third Class, and privately calls it what it is, the decoration handed to men who are not quite anybody. Neither servant nor equal, he goes down to Hungary with the household for twelve years.
suggested_refs: Wikipedia, 'Goedoelloe Palace', on the annual royal residence 1867-1918
sources: Dossier reconstruction for Menger's presence and the decoration
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godollo_Palace (coordinates and royal usage)

stops.name: Paris, the continental study tour
stops.date_confidence: attested that Menger undertook European and British study travel with Crown Prince Rudolf in 1877 and 1878 (Deutsche Biographie; University of Vienna faculty history, extensive study trips through Europe in 1877 and 1878). The specific Paris-Calais-London itinerary is dossier detail and the Calais crossing is not carried as a stop. Coordinate is the canonical Paris pin, inherited unaltered. Month set to December to place the stop in the stated winter.
stops.campa: The Crown Prince's continental study tour crosses France in winter with a party of court officials, the tutor among them. Paris under the young Third Republic is rebuilding its self-respect after Sedan and the Commune, and the Habsburg party moves through it as visiting royalty does, seeing what it is shown. Nothing Menger wrote about Paris survives in the sources that record the trip. Only the itinerary does. He was there, in the winter of 1877 into 1878, at the age of thirty-seven.
suggested_refs: Court travel accounts for Crown Prince Rudolf's study tour, winter 1877-1878
sources: Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html
University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at

stops.name: London, Quaritch's shop in Piccadilly
stops.date_confidence: the England travel is attested (University of Vienna faculty history; the dossier's Britannica citation for travels including to England could not be re-read, HTTP 403). The visit to Bernard Quaritch's antiquarian bookshop is dossier detail alone and is reconstruction nested inside an attested trip. The library figure of about 25,000 volumes is Menger's own 1911 estimate and is independently corroborated by German Wikipedia. Coordinate is the canonical London pin, inherited unaltered; the shop's own address is not used. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: In London he goes to Bernard Quaritch's shop in Piccadilly, then the great antiquarian bookselling house of Europe. England is also the country whose classical economists he is dismantling in print: Adam Smith's account of value, inherited by Ricardo and by the whole school after him, is the thing his own book was written against. He buys from the English booksellers regardless, and buys heavily. The library he is assembling will reach twenty-five thousand volumes by his own count in 1911.

stops.name: Vienna, the pamphlet signed Friedrich Saalfelden
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The anonymous 48-page pamphlet Der oesterreichische Adel und sein constitutioneller Beruf, the pseudonym, the two authors' arrangement to be abroad at publication, and the later dispute over how much of the text was Menger's are dossier detail, not independently corroborated in this pass. The dossier itself flags the authorship share as contested between Brigitte Hamann and Karl Menger, and that contradiction is left standing. Month set to April to order the segment.
stops.campa: A forty-eight page pamphlet appears in Vienna under the name Friedrich Saalfelden, Der oesterreichische Adel und sein constitutioneller Beruf, telling the Austrian nobility that it is idle, useless and constitutionally derelict. The author is the Crown Prince. The prose, or some share of it, is his tutor's. Both men arrange to be out of the country when it is published, and the outrage lands on a pseudonym. How much of the text was Menger's was still being argued a century later, by his own son on one side and Rudolf's biographer on the other.
suggested_refs: Der oesterreichische Adel und sein constitutioneller Beruf, Munich 1878, published under the pseudonym Friedrich Saalfelden
sources: Dossier reconstruction; the authorship share is internally contested between Hamann and Karl Menger and is not resolved

stops.name: Vienna, ordentlicher Professor
stops.date_confidence: attested for February 1879 by both the University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie. The declined calls to Karlsruhe, Basel and Zurich are dossier detail. The coordinate is the Ringstrasse main building, which did not open until 1884; his 1879 lecture rooms were still in the old university. The pin anticipates the site of the longer tenure rather than the exact 1879 venue, and is used consistently for the faculty stops from here on.
stops.campa: Franz Joseph signs the appointment: ordentlicher Professor at the University of Vienna, in February, after Menger has declined calls to Karlsruhe, Basel and Zurich. He will hold the chair for twenty-four years and teach from it nearly every economist who matters in the next Austrian generation. The imperial hand on the paper belongs to the father of the young man Menger has spent three years teaching. That is not why the appointment is made. It is not nothing, either.
stops.quote: Value is therefore nothing inherent in goods, no property of them, but merely the importance that we first attribute to the satisfaction of our needs, that is, to our lives and well-being, and in consequence carry over to economic goods as the exclusive causes of the satisfaction of our needs.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter III section 1, p. 116
suggested_refs: The imperial appointment decree of February 1879, University of Vienna archives
sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at
Deutsche Biographie, deutsche-biographie.de/gnd118580841.html

stops.name: Vienna, the curtain pulled aside
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The seance, the painter Hans Canon, the exposure of the medium, and Rudolf's request that Menger publish a notice are dossier detail with no independent corroboration reached. Month set to March to order the stop before the deanship in the same year.
stops.campa: At a spiritualist sitting in Vienna, Menger and the painter Hans Canon take hold of the curtain and pull it aside, exposing the medium at work. It is the decade in which educated Vienna is tilting tables and photographing ectoplasm. Rudolf, who detests the fashion, asks his old tutor to put the exposure into print, and Menger obliges. The professor of value, whose whole theory turns on what a man believes about his own needs, stands in a darkened room with a fistful of curtain in his hand.
suggested_refs: Menger's published notice on the seance, at Crown Prince Rudolf's request, 1881
sources: Dossier reconstruction, not independently corroborated

stops.name: Vienna, the first deanship
stops.date_confidence: attested, with a correction. The University of Vienna faculty history gives an academic year, 1881/82, not the calendar year 1881 the dossier recorded. The term is therefore autumn 1881 to summer 1882 and the date is set to October 1881 to reflect that.
stops.campa: He serves his first term as dean of the Faculty of Law and State Sciences, over the academic year running from the autumn of 1881 into the summer of 1882. The faculty is a law faculty; economics sits inside it as a guest discipline, taught to future officials and judges who will spend their careers administering an empire of eleven nationalities and one treasury. Menger, who came into the building through the law himself, now signs its papers. He will do this once more, seven years on.

stops.name: Vienna, the Untersuchungen and the Irrthuemer
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1883 Untersuchungen ueber die Methode der Socialwissenschaften (University of Vienna faculty history; Mises Institute biography) and for the 1884 Die Irrthuemer des Historismus in der deutschen Nationaloekonomie addressed to Schmoller (Mises Institute biography). Schmoller's dismissive review is attested in outline; the detail that he physically returned the copy unread with a printed note is dossier tradition. Day and month defaulted to 01-01.
stops.campa: He publishes the Untersuchungen: an argument that economics has laws which are not historical, that institutions such as money and language and law arise unintended out of individual action, and that the German Historical School's accumulation of particulars is not a science. Gustav Schmoller reviews it dismissively. Menger answers in 1884 with the Irrthuemer des Historismus, a set of open letters, and Schmoller sends his copy back unread. The quarrel takes the name Methodenstreit, and it costs Menger the German universities for a generation.
stops.quote: Let this work be regarded, therefore, as a friendly greeting from a collaborator in Austria, and as a faint echo of the scientific suggestions so abundantly lavished on us Austrians by Germany through the many outstanding scholars she has sent us and through her excellent publications.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Author's Preface, closing lines, p. 49, signed 'Dr. Carl Menger', written in 1871, twelve years before the quarrel

Die Irrthuemer des Historismus in der deutschen Nationaloekonomie, Vienna 1884

stops.name: Vienna, Zur Theorie des Kapitals
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1888 publication of Zur Theorie des Kapitals and for its disputing Boehm-Bawerk's definition of capital (Mises Institute biography). Boehm-Bawerk's three terms as finance minister and his theory of interest are general biographical record, not drawn from a source in the verified pool. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He publishes Zur Theorie des Kapitals against Boehm-Bawerk's definition of capital, which puts him in dispute with his own most powerful follower. Boehm-Bawerk is a Menger man, will hold the finance ministry three times, and will build the theory of interest on which the school's reputation abroad chiefly rests. Menger thinks he has abstracted the word away from what a businessman means by it, which is a sum of money in a going concern. Neither man moves.

stops.name: Vienna, the second deanship
stops.date_confidence: attested, with the same correction as the first term: the University of Vienna faculty history gives the academic year 1888/89, not the calendar year 1888 the dossier recorded. Date set to October 1888 to reflect the academic year.
stops.campa: The second deanship runs through the academic year from the autumn of 1888 into the summer of 1889, seven years after the first. He holds by now everything the empire can give an academic: the chair, the faculty, students who will carry the doctrine into the next century, and a former pupil who is to be emperor. He signs the papers, examines the candidates, administers the faculty of law and state sciences. He is forty-eight years old. The term still has months to run when the news comes down from Mayerling.

segments.name: Mayerling, and Money Without a Legislator

stops.name: Vienna, word from Mayerling
stops.date_confidence: Rudolf's death at Mayerling on 30 January 1889 is public historical record and consistent with the tutorship timeline. Menger's own reaction, the phrase about an ingenious man and a heavy loss, and the private lament about sacrifices that had not advanced his work are dossier-sourced and uncorroborated. Menger himself was in Vienna, not at Mayerling, which is why the stop sits at his own pin.
stops.campa: On the thirtieth of January the Crown Prince kills his mistress and himself at a hunting lodge at Mayerling, and the court spends three days constructing a story about heart failure before it concedes. Menger is in Vienna. Asked about his former pupil he calls him an ingenious man and a heavy loss, and says it in the register a professor uses. Privately he sets down something else: that he had given years to that education, that the years had not advanced his own work, and that the pupil is dead.

stops.name: Vienna, On the Origin of Money goes to London
stops.date_confidence: attested that Menger published 'On the Origin of Money' in the Economic Journal in 1892, translated by Caroline A. Foley (Econlib, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics). The essay was not fetched directly in this pass; the argument is quoted from the corresponding chapter of the 1871 book, which was read. The stop sits at Menger's own Vienna pin: the article travelled to London, he did not. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: The Economic Journal in London prints On the Origin of Money, translated by Caroline Foley, and the argument is the one from chapter eight of the 1871 book carried out to its end. Money was not decreed. It emerged because some goods are easier to sell than others, and each man, pursuing only his own advantage, takes the more saleable good in exchange whether he wants it for use or not, until one good is taken by everybody. No agreement was made. No law was passed.
stops.quote: Money is not an invention of the state. It is not the product of a legislative act.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter VIII section 1, p. 261. Verified in this translation of the 1871 book; a companion formulation appears in the 1892 Economic Journal article, which was not fetched, so the citation is to the copy actually read.
suggested_refs: Carl Menger, 'On the Origin of Money', Economic Journal 2 (1892), trans. Caroline A. Foley
sources: Econlib, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, 'Carl Menger'
Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz

stops.name: Vienna, the Currency Enquete Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1892 that Menger testified before the Austro-Hungarian currency commission (Mises Institute page on Menger's monetary writings; the dossier's Britannica citation returned HTTP 403 and could not support anything). The exact span 8 to 17 March 1892 appears in no source that could be read here and is demoted to reconstruction; the month is retained only as ordering. The hearing-room coordinate is an inferred general Vienna pin.
stops.campa: Austria-Hungary is preparing to leave its silver-linked paper currency for gold, and the Waehrungs-Enquete-Kommission calls the professor. The man who has just argued in London that money is no invention of the state spends the spring advising the state on how to invent its next one. On his own theory that is not a contradiction. He testifies at length: for a managed transition, against haste, and without treating gold as anything more than the commodity history happened to make most saleable.
stops.quote: As each economizing individual becomes increasingly more aware of his economic interest, he is led by this interest, without any agreement, without legislative compulsion, and even without regard to the public interest, to give his commodities in exchange for other, more saleable, commodities, even if he does not need them for any immediate consumption purpose.
stops.quote_source: Carl Menger, Principles of Economics, trans. Dingwall and Hoselitz, Chapter VIII section 1, p. 260

stops.name: Meran, the spa and the fishing society
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The recurring Meran trips from about 1880 and the membership in the Austrian Fishing Society are dossier detail with no independent corroboration reached. The date is set to June 1893 purely to place a recurring habit somewhere in the sequence; it marks no single documented visit.
stops.campa: He goes to Meran in the South Tyrol for the air and the water, as Austrians of his standing do, and he fishes. The membership in the Austrian Fishing Society is not decorative; he keeps it up for years. The neurasthenia and the ear disorder that will end his teaching are already in him, and the spa is the standing Habsburg answer to a nervous system that has stopped cooperating. A heavy, bearded, formal man stands in a river in the mountains, doing nothing at all.

stops.name: Vienna, Hofrat and the honorary degrees
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Neue Deutsche Biographie: the title of Hofrat and an honorary doctorate from Budapest in 1896, an honorary doctorate from Prague in 1899. Whether Menger travelled to Budapest or Prague to receive either is not recorded anywhere reached, which is why both are placed at his own Vienna pin rather than staged in those cities. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: The empire gives him the title Hofrat, imperial councillor, and Budapest gives him an honorary doctorate the same year. Prague follows in 1899. These are the honors a state pays a man it has decided is safe, and they arrive while the Methodenstreit is still costing him Berlin and Leipzig. In Vienna he is an institution; across the German border, where the Historical School holds every chair that matters, he is a foreign quarrel. Whether he went to either city to collect the parchment is not recorded.
suggested_refs: Honorary doctorate records, Budapest 1896 and Prague 1899

stops.name: Vienna, life member of the Herrenhaus
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1900 by the University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie. The brief association with the Constitutional Party group, the listing as independent by 1907, and the nominal participation are dossier detail. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He is made a life member of the Herrenhaus, the upper house of the Reichsrat, where the emperor seats archbishops, magnates and men of distinction who are expected to be reliable. He sits briefly with the Constitutional Party group and is listed as independent by 1907. His participation is nominal. What he had to say about how an empire should handle its money he had said to a commission, in writing, eight years earlier. The chamber meets to ratify what has been decided elsewhere.

sources: University of Vienna faculty history, geschichte.univie.ac.at

stops.name: Vienna, the birth of Karl Menger
stops.date_confidence: attested. Econlib identifies Karl Menger as Carl's son and a mathematician; English Wikipedia gives the birth as 13 January 1902 in Vienna and the death as 5 October 1985 at Highland Park, Illinois. The mother is not named in any source reached, and the dossier's report that the households were separate until about 1912/13 is reconstruction. The Menger sponge and the dimension work are general mathematical record, not drawn from the verified pool.
stops.campa: A son is born in Vienna on the thirteenth of January and named Karl. Menger is sixty-one. The two households, the father's and the child's, are separate, and stay separate for a decade. The boy will become a mathematician, will work on the definition of dimension and give his name to the Menger sponge, and will die at Highland Park, Illinois, on the fifth of October 1985. He is also the son who will edit his father's unfinished revision into a second edition. His mother is named in none of the records reached.
suggested_refs: Karl Menger's own account of his father, in the Carl Menger Papers, Duke University
sources: Econlib, Concise Encyclopedia of Economics, 'Carl Menger'

stops.name: Vienna, early retirement from the chair
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1903 and for its being at his own request by the University of Vienna faculty history and the Neue Deutsche Biographie. The reasons given, declining health, neurasthenia and an ear disorder, and Friedrich von Wieser's succession, are dossier detail. The honorary doctorate in law is dated 1909/10 by the University of Vienna and is folded into this stop rather than given one of its own. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: Citing declining health, neurasthenia and a disorder of the ear, he asks to be released from lecturing and retires early in 1903, at sixty-three, with eighteen years of life ahead of him. The petition is his own; nobody pushed him out, and he has been lecturing in the faculty since 1872. The chair he had held for twenty-four years passes to Friedrich von Wieser. Menger does not stop working; he stops appearing. In the academic year 1909 into 1910 the university gives him an honorary doctorate in law.

stops.name: Vienna, the rescript that gave the boy his name
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The imperial legitimation of Karl by rescript in April 1911 and the joining of the two households by about 1912/13 are dossier detail, not independently corroborated in this pass. The library figure of about 25,000 volumes by Menger's own 1911 estimate is independently corroborated by German Wikipedia.
stops.campa: By imperial rescript in April the boy is legitimated and may bear his father's surname. Menger is seventy-one; the son is nine. An arrangement kept quiet for a decade is closed by a piece of paper from the Emperor, which is how status is conferred in an empire. Within a year or two the two households become one, and the child moves in among the twenty-five thousand volumes his father counted that same year, into rooms where the books have taken every wall.

stops.name: Vienna, two cartons of letters
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction resting on a single family report. The burning of two cartons of correspondence and the remark that he was burning his own biography are attributed by the dossier to Karl Menger's testimony and have no independent corroboration. The surviving papers are at Duke University; the dossier's claim of 28 boxes described in a finding aid by Mason Barnett is corrected below and not carried here. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: He carries two cartons of correspondence to the fire and burns them. His son, ten or eleven years old and present, records what his father said while he did it: that he was burning his own biography. Decades of letters go into the stove, from colleagues and from rivals, from the court, from the Crown Prince. What he chose to leave is at Duke University now, in the special collections of the old William R. Perkins Library, and nobody knows what was in the two cartons.

stops.name: Vienna, a doctorate in political science under the republic
stops.date_confidence: attested for the academic year 1919/20 by the University of Vienna faculty history (Dr. rer. pol. h.c.). The dossier attached a superlative to it, that this was the first such degree ever conferred, sourced to the Neue Deutsche Biographie; the NDB page fetched contains no such phrase and the University of Vienna does not describe the degree as a first. The superlative is dropped. Date set to October 1919 to reflect the academic year.
stops.campa: The empire is gone. The Reichsrat is gone and the Herrenhaus with it, and the currency he once advised on is being destroyed by an inflation that will run into the millions. In the academic year 1919 into 1920 the University of Vienna gives him an honorary doctorate in political science. He is seventy-nine years old and has not lectured in sixteen years. The republic that confers the degree holds six million people; the empire that made him Hofrat held fifty.

stops.name: Vienna, the last illness among the books
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The uremic illness, the withdrawal through the war years, the revision of the money article and the annotated interleaved copies of the Grundsaetze are dossier detail; the fetched institutional sources confirm only the death date and city. Menger's refusal to permit reprints in his lifetime is independently attested by English Wikipedia.
stops.campa: A uremic illness enters its final phase. He is eighty years old. He has spent the war years and the collapse withdrawn among his books, revising the money article and annotating interleaved copies of the Grundsaetze that he would not permit anyone to reprint. Fifty years after the book made a school, the second edition he had promised in place of it does not exist and will not. The annotated copies are on the desk in February 1921, and he is still working on them.

stops.name: Vienna, death in the house at eighty-one
stops.date_confidence: attested for 26 February 1921 in Vienna by the Neue Deutsche Biographie and the University of Vienna faculty history. The early hours and the death at home are dossier detail. The interval of three days after his birthday holds only on the 23 February birth date; on the disputed 28 February date he would have died before his eighty-first birthday, which is one reason the contradiction matters.
stops.campa: Carl Menger dies at home in Vienna in the early hours of the twenty-sixth of February, three days after his eighty-first birthday. He had published one book that mattered, in 1871, and had spent fifty years failing to replace it. The theory of value inside it, that a thing is worth what it is worth to somebody, is by then the ordinary way economics is done across half the world, taught by men who never read him because they had read his students.

Vienna in 1921 is hungry, broke and stripped of an empire, and it buries him properly anyway. stops.name: Vienna, the edition his son assembled
stops.date_confidence: attested that Karl Menger edited a posthumous second German edition of the Grundsaetze in 1923 from his father's revision manuscripts, and that the English translation by Dingwall and Hoselitz appeared in 1950 (English Wikipedia). The Hayek-edited four-volume Gesammelte Werke of 1933-36 is carried at reconstruction: the Mises Institute page on that edition returned HTTP 404 and it could not be sourced independently. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: Karl Menger assembles a second German edition of the Grundsaetze out of his father's revision manuscripts and publishes it in 1923. It is a reconstruction from working papers, not a book its author approved, and it is the version much of Europe reads for a generation. The English translation his father had refused in his lifetime appears in 1950, by James Dingwall and Bert Hoselitz, seventy-nine years after Braumueller. F. A. Hayek had by then edited four volumes of collected works, printed between 1933 and 1936, which restored the unrevised text of 1871.

stops.campa: The twenty-five thousand volumes go to Hermina Andermann, who sells them, and the collection leaves Europe for Japan. A great part of it is at Hitotsubashi University, catalogued as the Menger Collection: the working library of the man who argued that a good's value is nothing but the importance a person attaches to it, valued in the end by a buyer on the other side of the world. What Andermann was paid, and in what year the crates were shipped, the reachable record does not say.

stops.name: Vienna, the relief in the arcaded courtyard
stops.date_confidence: attested by the University of Vienna faculty history: a relief portrait by Alfred Hoffmann unveiled in the Arkadenhof in 1929, funded by a committee of friends and former students; a commemorative plaque on the honor roll in the law faculty's entrance hall in 1950; a gate named jointly for Carl Menger and his son Karl in 1998/99. All three are posthumous and Menger was at none of them; they are carried here because they stand at his own university. Day and month defaulted.
stops.campa: In 1929, eight years after his death, a committee of his friends and former students pays for a relief portrait by Alfred Hoffmann and sets it in the arcaded courtyard of the university, among the faces the institution has decided it is made of. In 1950, the year an English translation of the Grundsaetze finally appears, his name goes onto the honor roll in the law faculty's entrance hall in Vienna. In 1998 the university names a gate for him and for his son together, the economist and the mathematician cut on one stone.
